title: Crucible.app Live Fleet Observability Decision Trace

events.summary: Replace the ambiguous CodexBar directional-reference language with a selective adopt, adapt, and reject policy for the Crucible.app foundation.

decision.rationale: Calling CodexBar merely directional preserved the no-copy boundary but lost the useful judgment. Crucible.app should reuse field-tested menu bar lifecycle, state, refresh, and testing lessons while adapting the entire data boundary to one Crucible CLI client and refusing CodexBar-specific provider, probe, helper, widget, and release complexity.

result.learning: A reference project is safest when its transferable lessons and non-transferable product complexity are both explicit; otherwise directional guidance either becomes decorative or quietly turns into architecture parity.

events.summary: Clarify that a fresh partial fleet snapshot advances the visible state when it is not older, while older snapshots are ignored and stale, failed, unavailable, or incompatible deliveries cannot replace newer known state.

decision.rationale: Merged-main runtime proof showed that treating every incomplete response as unusable froze the first partial snapshot indefinitely: Studio1 and Pro16 remained visibly offline after the CLI reported them available. The app must consume newer CLI truth without calling partial coverage live, ignore out-of-order snapshots without invalidating a newer presentation, and preserve newer known state across stale or failed deliveries.

result.learning: Freshness and completeness are independent dimensions: partial data can be the newest authoritative observation, so the app should advance it with explicit incompleteness rather than freezing or pretending it is complete.

events.summary: Require all-major notification mode to consume durable CLI-supplied transition events rather than infer lifecycle changes by comparing point-in-time snapshots.

links.title: CRUMAC-8 Add important and major-state notifications

decision.rationale: A five-minute snapshot cadence can miss transitions that begin and end between polls, while fresh partial snapshots can temporarily omit entities and manufacture false diffs. Stable condition identities are sufficient for active boundary episodes, but the promise of all major state changes requires an ordered replay window or cursor, CLI-authored importance, and stable event identities. Keeping that intelligence in the CLI preserves the sole-front-door boundary and gives agents and Crucible.app the same operational history.

linked_artifacts.title: CRUMAC-15 Expose durable major fleet transitions for notification replay

result.learning: A snapshot can truthfully describe current state but cannot guarantee delivery of transient events. Alert-mode promises must be matched to the temporal semantics and replay guarantees of their source contract.
